text: Mara finds it at 3:12 every Thursday, the book, in the bread rack. Its always the same. The Practical Guide to Inland Birds. Spine cracked and blue, stamp from a library forty miles away. She puts it on the flour bin. Wipes butter off it. Means to return it after shift. Never does. By noon, the errands, the heat, the sleep, eat it. Next Thursday, there it is, tucked between cooling rye loaves. Tonight. The bakery hums. Proofing cabinet and old radio static. Rain on the front window, silver lines. She lifts it, both hands, as if it might be warm. There's a receipt folded on the heron chapter. She opens it. I think you are the only person awake when I am. Block letters. Page 47. She turns. Grey heron, marsh, one foot up. Patient as a saint. Pencil below. Thursday, 3:30? The clock over the mixer ticks. Mara brushes flour off her apron. Unlocks the door. Turns on the little open sign.
